TEXT_F:
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001: “Time for Common Sense” — Summary

Core vision
- Trust people over government: devolve power, cut taxes and regulation, and free public services from political micromanagement.
- Strengthen families, local institutions, charities, and national identity; be “in Europe, not run by Europe.”

Families and education
- Tax cuts focused on early years: raise Children’s Tax Credit by £200; new Married Couple’s Allowance (transferable personal allowance) worth up to £1,000 for families with children under 11 or carers; remove tax on widowed parents’ allowances; reform Working Families Tax Credit to pay the caring parent.
- Create “Free Schools”: full autonomy for heads/governors; less bureaucracy; easier exclusions with Progress Centres for disruptive pupils; more per‑pupil funding direct to schools; allow successful schools to expand and new faith/parent/charity/company schools to open; parents can trigger Ofsted and management change.
- Universities: endowment funds for independence; no top‑up fees; student loan repayments only above £20,000 income.

Crime and justice
- More police; cut red tape; visible policing (“cops in shops”) and parish constables; target antisocial behaviour.
- Persistent young offenders: 10x more Secure Training Centre places; link release to qualifications/behaviour.
- Tougher drug laws: mandatory jail for dealing to under‑16s; harsher near schools.
- Honest sentencing (end automatic and special early release); prisoners to work; lifetime supervision possible for sex offenders; protect children online.
- Strengthen victims’ rights and clarify self‑defence/double jeopardy.

Economy and tax
- £8bn annual tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish tax on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; cut petrol/diesel duty by 6p; restore Married Couple’s Allowance; business reliefs; abolish IR35.
- Simpler, more transparent public accounts; National Accounts Commission; clearer tax statements.
- Deregulation: independent Deregulation Commission with departmental regulatory budgets; exemptions for small firms; scrap Climate Change Levy package; review nuclear.
- Keep the pound; strengthen BoE MPC independence; Council of Economic Advisers; spending growth within trend GDP.

Health
- Match NHS spending plans but end micromanagement; Patient’s Guarantee: clinically set maximum waits (starting with cancer/cardiac), with choice of NHS or private treatment if breached.
- Restore ward sister/matron authority; GP and patient choice of hospital; encourage GP specialisation; allow proven complementary therapies; increase hospice funding; expand high-throughput surgical units; Exceptional Medicines Fund for costly drugs.

Older people and care
- Cut tax on savings; raise age allowance; increase basic pension (extra for over‑75s); optional consolidation of winter fuel/TV licence into higher, tax‑free pension.
- Abolish compulsory annuity purchase at 75; explore funded pension option for young workers; protect assets of those who pre‑fund long‑term care.

Europe, defence, and asylum
- Keep veto; reject euro; renegotiate Nice; embed “reserved powers” in UK law; complete single market; tackle EU fraud.
- Back NATO; oppose EU army outside NATO; meet full manning; exempt forces from ECHR; support missile defence; maintain independent deterrent.
- Asylum: secure reception centres until decisions; presume refusal from safe countries; dedicated Removals Agency.

Welfare and civil society
- Office of Civil Society; abolish charities’ irrecoverable VAT (funded by euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with “Britain Works,” paying providers for jobs gained and sustained; “Can Work, Must Work.”
- Expect lone parents with children 11+ to seek suitable work; better savings rules and return‑to‑work support for disabled; national anti‑fraud squad; clean up NI numbers.

Town, country, transport, environment
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; clearer food origin labelling; cut rural business rates; support post offices via benefit card; abolish top‑down housebuilding targets; “Blue Belts” for waterways; urban Regeneration Companies; expand homeownership.
- Transport: 6p fuel duty cut; long-term investment; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries (Brit Disc); revive rail; support London Underground reform.

Culture, media, sport
- £3bn endowment for arts/heritage (Channel 4 privatisation + Lottery surpluses); boost tourism; protect school sport and playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; single communications regulator; liberalise ownership; fair BBC regulation.

Constitution and governance
- Devolve power to best councils (“free councils”); local referendums for big tax rises; scrap regional agencies/assemblies; English Votes for English Laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and elected element; tougher Commons scrutiny; keep FPTP; reduce ministers/MPs/spads; uphold Belfast Agreement with decommissioning.

TEXT_G:
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 — Summary (≤500 words)

Core stance
- SNP stands for Scottish independence and putting Scotland’s interests first. More SNP MPs strengthen the case for an independence referendum; a majority would trigger one. Meanwhile, SNP MPs will press for more powers for the Scottish Parliament and oppose anti-Scottish measures at Westminster.

Fiscal and investment framework
- Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations by investing surplus oil revenues to fund public services sustainably (modelled on Norway).
- Establish a Scottish Trust for Public Investment to finance infrastructure more cheaply than PFI/PPP.

Constitution and democracy
- Written constitution; proportional representation at all levels; inclusive citizenship. Retain the Queen as Head of State subject to a referendum. Reduce and democratise quangos; civil service opportunities expand with independence.

Education and young people
- Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants as resources allow. Votes at 16; establish a powerful Children’s Commissioner; implement UN CRC.
- Education Convention to depoliticise change; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18 in phases; end league tables; invest in school refurbishments via STPI; support Gaelic-medium education and inclusive schooling.

Economy, enterprise, tourism
- Tailored Scottish economic policy; invest in transport, broadband and skills; streamline development agencies; fold tourism into the enterprise network. Reorient tourism toward marketing Scotland and improve access, including better air links.

Work, pay and unions
- Devolve and refocus New Deal into a “Better Deal.” Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; develop offsets for small businesses. Charter of Trade Union Rights; support EU worker protections.

Environment, energy, water
- Environmental audit and National Environment Plan; empower SEPA over MoD sites. Target 12% of all energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear; lead in decommissioning. Promote “six Rs.” Review water charges and governance; halt backdoor privatisation.

Health and care
- Create a cross-party National Health Care Commission; end postcode treatment with binding HTBS decisions. Free fruit in primary schools and healthier school meals. Reintroduce free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges. Invest via STPI in modern equipment and hospitals; £4m Clean Hospitals Fund; recruit 1,500 nurses; aim to halve inpatient waiting times. Free personal care for all elderly.

Europe, defence, foreign affairs
- Pro-EU, anti-superstate; subsidiarity; euro adoption only by referendum when conditions suit. With independence: full EU representation. Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased NATO withdrawal while cooperating on peacekeeping; form a professional Scottish Defence Force. Create commercially focused overseas offices; raise aid to UN levels, cancel debt, untie aid.

Culture, language, media, sport
- Devolve broadcasting oversight; “Scottish Six”; support digital transition. Reform Scottish Arts Council; national theatre; Scottish Lottery; support Gaelic and Scots. Focus sports funding locally; support football academies; bid for Euro 2008.

Social justice, housing, communities
- National anti-poverty strategy and “poverty proofing.” End asylum voucher system; fast, fair assessment. Seek UK write-off of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via STPI; oppose wholesale stock transfer. Core funding and water-charge exemptions for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.

Law, order, drugs
- 1,000 additional police officers (£25m). Drugs: tougher on dealers; expand Drug Courts and treatment. Parental compensation orders for youth damage; lifelong supervision for high-risk sex offenders; implement MacLean Report; speed up courts; retain Scottish fines for justice reinvestment.

Tax and local government
- No overall tax rise without mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity. Immediate measures: cut fuel duty by 10p/gal, funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100,000. Review local government finance, including local income tax; PR (STV) for councils.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land
- Support small businesses, rural ICT, transport, and services; contingency funds for crises; cut fuel duty and tackle high rural prices. Post–FMD agricultural review; fair EU implementation; promote diversification and organics; renegotiate LFA. Fisheries: compensated tie-ups, conservation, devolved management via Zonal Councils; restore Scottish control over 6,000 sq miles; support processing and aquaculture; independent salmon-farming inquiry. Expand community land rights.

Pensions and social security
- Restore earnings link for basic pensions using NI surplus; move toward parity with MIG; cold climate allowance via weekly winter payments. Streamline benefits via a single agency; simplify housing benefit; improve take-up; extend winter fuel to severely disabled under 60 as resources allow; review support for 16–17s and WFTC cliff-edges.

Transport
- Secure fair UK investment; use STPI for lower-cost projects. Create Regional Transport Authorities; single safety body; take a public share in Railtrack. Reopen and electrify key lines (e.g., Borders, airport links, ECML); national concessionary travel; develop light rail; repair roads and fix bottlenecks (e.g., M74, A9); lower ferry fares toward Road Equivalent Tariff; expand direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.
